name: sloptells
title: sloptells (measured)
description: Tells from sloptells.com, a database that measures model output against register-matched pre-2022 human baselines and a canon of acclaimed prose, then dates each tell and tracks its lifecycle. Only active/saturated tells rated low collateral and expressible as a pattern were taken; formatting and cadence tells, and everything rated medium or high collateral, were left out. Ratios in each description are theirs.

rules.name: “genuinely”
rules.description: The intensifier models reach for to signal sincerity. Fifty-three times the human rate, and the highest-ratio tell measured. Measured at ×53 vs humans.
rules.suggest: Delete it. If the claim needs the word, the claim is not carrying itself.

hit: The thock with each press is genuinely addictive.
I'm genuinely excited for you to try it.
miss: The genuine article costs twice as much.

rules.name: “That said, …”
rules.description: The pivot connective used to perform balance, at nineteen times the human rate. Measured at ×19 vs humans.
rules.suggest: Cut it, or make the contrast explicit.

hit: The salt preserves it. That said, there are practical limits.
miss: Everything that said otherwise was wrong.

rules.name: “the real question is …”
rules.description: Reframing as insight: announcing what the real issue is, rather than stating it. Measured at ×30 vs humans.
rules.suggest: State the issue. Calling it the real one adds nothing.

hit: The real question to ask yourself is why you want to learn.
The real issue may not be shortages so much as logistics.
miss: A real question deserves a real answer.

rules.name: “here's what actually happened”
rules.description: The staged reveal, promising a payoff before delivering one. Measured at ×18 vs humans.
rules.suggest: Deliver the point without announcing it first.

hit: But here's what surprised me most: the first year was different.
miss: Here is what you asked for.

rules.name: “one of those X”
rules.description: False familiarity: filing the topic into a recognisable genre of situations the reader is assumed to share. Measured at ×12 vs humans.
rules.suggest: Describe this case rather than the genre.

hit: This is one of those rare boring-is-good moments.
It is one of those cases where the cache lies.
miss: She was one of those who stayed.

rules.name: “(this) feels like”
rules.description: Hedging with vibes: reporting an impression where a human states an opinion or a fact. Measured at ×12 vs humans.
rules.suggest: State the opinion, or the fact.

hit: This feels like a step change for the team.
It feels like the keyboard could double as a paperweight.

rules.name: “curious what others think”
rules.description: The engagement-bait closer, soliciting replies rather than ending. Measured at ×10 vs humans.
rules.suggest: End on the point. If you want replies, ask something specific.

hit: Curious what others think about this approach.
miss: I was curious how the parser handled it.

rules.name: “the actual X”
rules.description: Emphatic “actual” used to signal that the real thing is finally being named. Measured at ×8.2 vs humans.

hit: The actual failure mode is subtler than that.
miss: Actual costs came in under budget.

rules.name: “the privilege of …”
rules.description: Announced gratitude. Not observed in the human baseline at all. Measured at only in AI.
rules.suggest: Say what you did and with whom.

hit: I've had the privilege of working alongside talented people.
miss: Privilege escalation was the root cause.

rules.name: “X taught me Y”
rules.description: The lesson-extraction move that converts an anecdote into a moral. Measured at only in AI.
rules.suggest: Report what happened and let the reader draw the lesson.

hit: Closing those deals taught me something important.

rules.name: “The lesson? …”
rules.description: The rhetorical-question header that packages a conclusion. Measured at construct.
rules.suggest: State the conclusion as a sentence.

hit: The lesson? Ship earlier.
The real wins? Built my own routine.
miss: The lesson plan covered three topics.

rules.name: “Not because X. Because Y.”
rules.description: The negation-then-reason couplet, split across two sentences for cadence. Measured at construct.

hit: Not because I'm done. Because I'm finally starting.
miss: We stopped, not because it failed but because it finished.

rules.name: “You're not alone”
rules.description: Pre-emptive reassurance addressed to a reader who did not ask for it. Measured at only in AI.

hit: You're not imagining it: hiring really has slowed.
If the build feels slower, you're not alone.
miss: You are not alone in the building after six.

rules.name: “rather than”
rules.description: The 2026 flagship tell: models reach for “rather than” where humans write “instead of” or rephrase. Measured at ×5.0 vs humans.
rules.suggest: Write “instead of”, or rephrase so the contrast is not needed.

hit: The compounds dissolve in water rather than reaching your eyes.
miss: He would rather walk than wait.

rules.note: measured collateral: low, but it is ordinary English — expect this one to need calibration on technical prose
